subject: Feature-level unit economics: stitching token cost to CAC & payback
message_1_subject: Re: Follow-up — feature scoping & cost targets
message_1_body:
Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap from our side and a short list of asks so we can finalize the unit-econ worksheet for the pilot: 

Summary of what I heard:
- Pilot scope: 3 targeted features (clinical triage, appointment summarization, inbound message drafting).
- Expected active users: ~12k MAU, with ~400k messages/month across those features.
- Preferred commercial target: <$2,500 per 1M tokens (target you mentioned was a hard ceiling).

Key asks from us to finish the costing model: 
1) Confirm expected average prompt + response size for each feature (tokens per call). A rough ballpark is fine (e.g., triage = 350 tokens, summary = 800 tokens, draft = 200 tokens).
2) Monthly conversion path assumptions: what % of MAU will use each feature weekly?
3) Any internal margin or price-to-feature expectations (e.g., $/feature per month target, or CAC recovery window you want to see).

I attached a draft workbook (medpilot-feature-econ-workbook.xlsx) that maps tokens -> $/1M tiers, and rolls up $/feature + CAC payback scenarios. Once you confirm the three inputs above we can run three pricing scenarios (conservative / expected / aggressive) and show the payback timeline with a 6–18 month slider.

Next steps: if you can reply with the token estimates by EOD Thursday I’ll push the scenario outputs and a recommended pilot commitment band before our Friday sync.

Best,
Mateo
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
mateo@redwood.com
(Attachment: medpilot-feature-econ-workbook.xlsx)
message_2_subject: Re: Follow-up — feature scoping & cost targets
message_2_body:
Thanks Mateo — good summary. A few clarifications from our end: 

1) Token estimates (rough averages):
   - Clinical triage: 320 tokens per call (prompt+response)
   - Appointment summarization: 950 tokens per document
   - Drafting inbound reply: 220 tokens per reply

2) Usage assumptions:
   - Clinical triage: ~9% of MAU weekly (~1.1k weekly actives)
   - Summarization: 4% weekly
   - Drafting: 18% weekly

3) Commercial constraints:
   - We have a pilot budget earmarked at $65k over 3 months.
   - Decision-makers want to see CAC payback <= 9 months for any new feature buy (we're measuring incremental revenue per feature).
   - For pricing, $2,500 / 1M tokens is a hard ceiling; ideally we'd land closer to $1,800 / 1M tokens but we're flexible for committed capacity.

Can you show $/feature under both $1,800 and $2,500 / 1M token bands and a committed-capacity discount that would get us to the $1,800 equivalent? Also we need a quick note on inference margin impact (i.e., if your cost to serve is X, what's the expected gross margin at each price band).

Elena
Director, Product Operations
MedPilot Health
elena@medpilot.com
message_3_subject: Re: Follow-up — feature scoping & cost targets
message_3_body:
Hi Elena — great, thanks for the numbers. I ran the three scenario outputs in the attached workbook and pulled the headline unit-econ and payback notes below (see medpilot-feature-econ-workbook.xlsx for full math).

Headline unit economics (monthly rollups based on your usage assumptions):
- Aggregate tokens/month (estimate): 400k tokens/month (matches your 400k note) — workbook breaks down by feature.
- $/1M token price band implications: 
  • At $2,500 / 1M tokens -> estimated cost to MedPilot = $1,000 / month (pro rata) for pilot usage; translates to ~$0.40 per triage interaction, $0.95 per summarization, $0.18 per draft (see sheet 'per-feature').
  • At $1,800 / 1M tokens -> per-feature drops to ~ $0.29 triage, $0.68 summary, $0.13 draft.

Stitching to CAC and payback (assumptions used):
- We assumed lift-driven ARR per activated feature user: $12/user/year for triage, $6/user/year for summary, $9/user/year for drafting (we can tune).
- CAC as a blended sales+implementation cost for pilot-to-paid conversion: $45k (we used your pilot budget as a proxy and amortized expected conversion rates).
- Payback outcomes: under the $1,800 / 1M tokens band and the stated usage assumptions, median payback ~ 7.5 months. Under $2,500 / 1M tokens, median payback ~ 11 months. (Workbook tab 'payback' shows 6/9/12/18 month sensitivity).

Inference margin impact vs Redwood's cost: 
- Redwood internal assumed cost-to-serve (inference-only) for the rolled-up workload: ~$0.55 / 1M tokens (this is internal baseline we use for scenarioing; final numbers vary by quantization & batching on dedicated capacity).
- At $1,800 / 1M tokens price -> estimated gross margin ~ 69% on inference (excludes support/engineering).
- At $2,500 / 1M tokens -> estimated gross margin ~ 78%.

Committed capacity option to hit your $1,800 target: 
- 6-month reserved band at 1.0M tokens/month list-priced at $2,200 /1M with an upfront commit discount structure -> effectively nets to $1,760 /1M after usage credits.
- Alternatively, a 12-month term with tiered volume bands would net you to ~$1,700 /1M. We can formalize the exact structure in a one-page term sheet.

Recommended next steps (for Friday sync):
1) Confirm the lift assumptions per feature (I can update workbook quickly).
2) Decide which committed band you prefer (6-month or 12-month) so we can prepare a pilot term sheet.
3) If OK, Marissa (cc'd) will propose a pilot discount and SLA for the term sheet.

Visibility note: I've attached the workbook + a short pilot term-sheet stub (redwood-pilot-term-sheet.pdf). If you'd like, I can also run a fast sensitivity that substitutes a lower cognitive-lift number (conservative revenue) to show worst-case payback.

Best,
Mateo
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: medpilot-feature-econ-workbook.xlsx, redwood-pilot-term-sheet.pdf)
message_4_subject: Re: Follow-up — feature scoping & cost targets
message_4_body:
Thanks Mateo / Elena — quick internal note then customer-facing ask.

Internal: Mateo, the committed-band approach (6mo to net ~1,760 /1M) looks fine to propose given their pilot budget and the payback sensitivity. We should be prepared to show the 12-month alternative if they push for a lower net price.

Customer-facing (Elena): happy to propose the following as a pilot offer — 6-month reserved at effective $1,760 /1M tokens with a churn-protected conversion credit (applies only if they convert to a paid committed term within 90 days). Pilot terms will include a lightweight SLA for latency and an implementation checklist (2 week integration). I’ll draft the one-pager and circulate by EOD tomorrow.

Elena — does that structure sound like it would get you to 'OK to pilot' from your side? If yes, Mateo and I will push the formal pilot term and PO language.

—Marissa
VP, Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
